newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia board approves five-year fiscal plan.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia board approves five-year fiscal plan.

text.p: Philadelphia's oversight board on Tuesday unanimously approved a new five-year fiscal plan for the city, the agency's executive director said.

"We still have concerns about some of the revenue projections, especially riverboat gaming, and some of the expenditure cuts that are to be made in the out years," Joseph Vignola, executive director of the Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority, said in an interview.
City council approved the plan in March, and Mayor Ed Rendell signed it in April.

The state Legislature created PICA in 1991 to bail out the cash-strapped city and sell bonds to help balance its budget. Since, then PICA has overseen a string of balanced budgets as the city's economy recovered.
